newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline diffs ease on build.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline diffs ease on build.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline differentials eased Tuesday ahead of a report confirming perceptions refiners had built up stocks in the week leading up to the Thanksgiving Day holiday weekend, traders said.
The American Petroleum Institute said gasoline stocks in primary storage at PADD II Midwest refineries rose a net 1.7 million barrels compared to the prior week.
The build was fueled by a continued blistering pace of production at Midwest refineries, which were operating at 97.4 percent of capacity on the week, the trade group said.
Low sulphur diesel stocks were up 758,000 barrels compared to the same week last year, while high sulphur diesel supplies were off 1.39 million barrels year-to-year.
Differentials on late-month deliveries remained weaker in both markets, reflecting expectations of ample supplies available in the markets in the weeks ahead.
Group Three unleaded was bid 1.25 cent a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 2.0 cents under for later deliveries, with premium steady at 2.0 cents higher.
Chicago unleaded eased to 0.50/0.75 cent over the print for first-cycle deliveries and remained 1.25/1.0 cent under for later deliveries, with premium 2.75 cents higher.
Group Three early December low sulphur diesel differentials plunged 2.5 cents a gallon to bids 3.75 cents a gallon under the print, with later deliveries bid 4.0 cents a gallon under.
Chicago low sulphur diesel eased to 1.25/1.0 cent a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 2.25/2.0 cent a gallon under the print for later deliveries.
High sulphur diesel was bid 4.50 cents a gallon under the print in Group Three and1.75 cent a gallon under in Chicago.
